strategy.audience: DeFi liquidity providers, risk officers, and treasury managers seeking protection against shared bad debt contagion.
strategy.problem_statement: In shared liquidity lending pools, the primary failure mode of an undercollateralized or underwater position is contagion: when liquidations fail or experience slippage, the resulting bad debt is absorbed by the mutual reserve, haircutting passive depositors and spreading one actor's insolvency to the entire pool.
strategy.angle: Leverage is easy to obtain, but preventing cascading liquidations is where pooled architectures fail; mitigating systemic risk requires strict structural containment so that a single delinquent position cannot dilute or freeze mutual reserves.

briefs.problem_statement: In pooled lending models, collateral is locked into a shared liability pool where a single bad position socializes losses across all depositors, trapping capital as passive loss absorption rather than enabling it to perform productive, distinct jobs.
briefs.angle: Pooled lending forces collateral into an inefficient defensive stance, where instead of maximizing productivity and doing multiple jobs, assets sit idle or take collective haircuts to backstop unrelated defaults.
briefs.audience: DeFi liquidity providers, risk managers, and institutional allocators evaluating capital productivity versus pooled risk structures.
briefs.strongest_objection: Shared collateral pools aggregate liquidity depth more effectively than isolated or multi-utility structures, reducing slippage and ensuring high availability of borrowable assets despite mutualized contagion risk.

briefs.strongest_objection: Pooled lending models maximize capital efficiency and aggregate deep liquidity, whereas isolating risks can fragment available capital and potentially precipitate earlier liquidations during volatility due to thinner local liquidity.

briefs.problem_statement: Pooled lending models mutualize default risk across all participants, causing a single bad debt position or failed liquidation to haircut shared liquidity and compromise solvency for every user in the pool.
briefs.angle: Autonomous agents can execute payments programmatically, but they cannot safely borrow from pooled credit structures where third-party defaults expose the agent to unhedgeable, systemic contagion outside its algorithmic control.
briefs.audience: Developers and protocol architects building autonomous agents and on-chain credit systems on Stellar Soroban.
briefs.strongest_objection: Autonomous agents do not require specialized isolated credit primitives because their execution speed enables them to detect bad debt accrual and exit or hedge pooled risk faster than manual market participants.
